brief: GS flows note: hyperscaler earnings failed to resolve the AI funding/returns debate, so the AI pain trade continued; ex-AI risk appetite stays low pending midterms and an Iran decision. The broadening trade (SPXXAI) worked in October, but weaker growth would hit short-squeeze-driven pockets specifically. Five ideas follow. Midterms: a Democratic sweep favors ACA Beneficiaries (subsidies reauthorization aids hospitals/insurers) and AI Power (if power supply eases electricity inflation), but datacenter cost-sharing would hurt ex-Power hardware; corporate tax law likely holds through 2027-28 given Trump's veto power, with risk rising only beyond 2029. Uncorrelated trades: Healthcare AI Beneficiaries (low correlation to AI/rates/oil, YTD outperformer) and the systematic Growth Value Rotator (+27%/+18% YTD). Disruption: Software vs Semis up 88% from June lows and re-rated 17x to 23x P/E; Insurance's October defensive rally masks underappreciated cyber underwriting risk. Banks: Europe's worst month since March 2023 looks overdone given ROTE expansion; Greek Banks bought on NII beats and catalysts; Japanese Banks set up for a relief rally on a BoJ December hike signal. Defense: a 13% three-week bounce could extend toward a 30% re-rating.
